title: Scalar compatibility of fixed normalized tensor reindexing
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and an isomorphism g:X→Y with l invertible. Let D and T be normalized completion and tensor reindexing data at E satisfying their Laws. For every finite extension L of Q_l and every Q_l-algebra embedding iota:E→L, given normalized completion and tensor reindexing data Dprime,Tprime at L satisfying their Laws, there exists a PodReindexCoefficientTransition S from D to Dprime satisfying its Laws for these exact D,T,Dprime,Tprime: the balanced ordinary scalar generator formula, the full-system reduction square, the normalized limit square and the completed tensor square. Identity embeddings are included. Definitions: [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-pod-completion-reindex-models], [def-pod-completion-tensor-reindex-models], [def-pod-completion-tensor-normalization], [def-pod-completion-reindex-coefficient-transition], [def-pod-scalar-completion-tensor-comparisons].

proof.text: retain the supplied completion and tensor comparisons at E and L. On completed module sheaves scalar extension commutes with reindexing by balanced tensor associativity; normalize it to send a tensor x to the original a tensor x after the coefficient identification. The inverse is reverse relabelling. Finite free scalar extension preserves complete constructibility, including the common finite cohomological interval. Use the normalized scalar completion realizations at X and Y for S.source and S.target. On simultaneous quotient resolutions the reduction square is balanced tensor associativity and sends each generator to the same scalar tensor. The corresponding limit square is the diagonal scalar comparison on both Roos coordinates; its counit formula gives exactly podScalarLimit. On tensor towers, the two scalar/reindexing paths agree on every homogeneous pure tensor, commute with transitions, and have the same signed differential. Applying the full Roos realization and descending gives S.Laws, with the displayed podScalarReduction and podScalarLimit maps, rather than independent finite evaluations. In particular E=L and the identity embedding use these same formulas. Empty schemes and zero inputs introduce no additional hypotheses. .

theorem podReindexingTensorCoefficientTransition
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (D : PodCompletionReindex l E g) (hD : PodCompletionReindex.Laws l E g D)
    (T : PodCompletedTensorReindex l E g D)
    (hT : PodCompletedTensorReindex.Laws l E g D T)
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ_[l] L] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] L]
    (ι : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] L)
    (D' : PodCompletionReindex l L g) (hD' : PodCompletionReindex.Laws l L g D')
    (T' : PodCompletedTensorReindex l L g D')
    (hT' : PodCompletedTensorReindex.Laws l L g D' T') :
    ∃ S : PodReindexCoefficientTransition l E L ι g D D',
      S.Laws l E L ι g D D' T T'
